risks: Steel demand and spreads remain cyclical and exposed to construction, manufacturing, trade policy and raw-material costs.
Quarterly earnings can move sharply with steel pricing and utilization; the Helion mark is non-operating and should not be treated as core execution.
Physical steel demand is durable, but company returns remain sensitive to spreads, utilization and capital discipline on new capacity.
Steel spreads and utilization can reverse quickly with construction/manufacturing cycles and trade-policy changes.
Non-operating investment marks can inflate reported earnings and confidence if not separated from core operating performance.
Steel-cycle reversal and project-return uncertainty can compress earnings.
